record.original_question: Is every topological disk in R^3 with constant mean curvature and circular boundary necessarily either a planar disk or a spherical cap?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.8 (5*). Is a topological cmc disk spanning a circle a planar disk or a spherical cap?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $\Sigma \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a compact, immersed surface of constant mean curvature (CMC) whose underlying topological type is that of a closed disk, and assume that the boundary $\partial \Sigma$ is a round circle in some plane of $\mathbb{R}^3$. Must $\Sigma$ be either a flat planar disk bounded by that circle (in the case of zero mean curvature) or a spherical cap bounded by that circle (in the case of nonzero mean curvature)?
artifact.status_search_result: This is the classical "spherical cap conjecture" for CMC topological disks bounded by a circle. It remains a well-known open problem in differential geometry. Partial results are known under additional hypotheses such as embeddedness combined with local convexity, or stability (where umbilical caps are the only stable immersed CMC disks with circular boundary), but the general case is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: An extension of Liebmann's Theorem to hypersurfaces with boundary
status_evidence.snippet: A locally convex, embedded, compact, connected CMC hypersurface bounded by a circle in Euclidean space is necessarily a spherical cap, providing a positive answer to the conjecture under the additional assumption of local convexity.
status_evidence.claim: The spherical cap conjecture is open in general; partial results exist under added convexity hypotheses.

status_evidence.title: Surfaces with constant mean curvature in Euclidean space (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Whether spherical caps and discs are the only compact CMC surfaces bounded by a circle ... remains wide open.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture for CMC topological disks spanning a circle remains open.
